article_title: Spatial cognition in minimally invasive surgery: a systematic review.
citation: Vajsbaher Tina, Schultheis Holger, Francis Nader K. (2018). Spatial cognition in minimally invasive surgery: a systematic review. BMC Surgery. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12893-018-0416-1
title: Visual working memory as a holistic framework for spatial cognition in MIS learning and performance
description: The review proposes shifting from studying isolated spatial abilities to a holistic account centered on working memory, the active 'mental workspace' that temporarily processes incoming stimuli, maintains focus, blocks unnecessary information and delegates cognitive processes. The component "responsible for processing and manipulating visuospatial stimuli is referred to as VWM". In MIS, novices' repeated gaze switches between monitor and instruments raise attentional demands, reduce effective WM capacity and produce cognitive overload; the framework aims to explain fragmentary findings on VSA, mental rotation and mental practice within one system.
requirements: Research and training must consider the functioning of the whole WM system rather than isolated spatial abilities
External and internal factors influencing the surgeon must be considered together
constraints: The framework is a theoretical narrative proposed by the authors; the review states its validity in practice still needs to be tested
target_learners: novice surgeons and surgical trainees learning minimally invasive surgery
target_learning_goals: intraoperative spatial orientation and attention allocation
reduction of cognitive load during surgery
examples: The review explains novice laparoscopic performance through simultaneous WM demands: retaining procedure steps, transforming the 2D image into a 3D representation, retrieving operative knowledge, and tracking instrument coordination
key_sources: Vajsbaher Tina, Schultheis Holger, Francis Nader K. (2018). Spatial cognition in minimally invasive surgery: a systematic review. BMC Surgery. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12893-018-0416-1
